summary: Implement 15 code changes across 4 phases to improve QuantFlow win rate from ~40-50% to 55-65% by fixing 3 architectural gaps: (1) no profit-taking exits, (2) overly restrictive AND-entry logic, (3) Sharpe-only validation pipeline.
approach: Sequential 4-wave execution — Phase 1 creates shared infrastructure (optimizer win_rate objective, gate win_rate support, profit_target_exit function, param_space JSONs), Phase 2 relaxes entry conditions with min_conditions count-based logic, Phase 3 wires profit targets and improves exit logic across all 6 templates, Phase 4 upgrades the signal pipeline with strength-weighted consolidation and per-strategy risk budgets. Each phase builds on the previous; backward compatibility is preserved via defaults that match current behavior.

stages: Phase 1: Add win_rate objective + profit_target_exit + param_space JSONs (shared foundation)
Phase 2: Refactor 3 template entries from AND to count-based min_conditions
Phase 3: Wire profit_target_exit + trailing stops + RSI-adaptive targets into 6 templates
Phase 4: Strength-weighted consolidation + per-strategy risk budgets + actual win_rate sizing

design_decisions: profit_target_exit() placed in _runtime.py alongside existing numeric helpers for shared access
min_conditions defaults preserve current behavior: trend=4, mean_rev=2, vol_breakout=5 (all conditions required)
param_space JSONs complement existing YAML configs — YAML for runtime params, JSON for optimizer search spaces
Strength-weighted consolidation uses strategy_hit_rates dict (default 0.5 for unknown strategies)
Per-strategy risk budgets use win_rate proportional allocation within RiskEngine

patterns: profit target exit with max holding bars
